doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Family roots, South Side and early training
title: Her first Chicago nightclub gig on 55th Street
summary: She thinks she first worked the 65 Club or Swingland on 55th Street, where she was not the main act but had a complete show around her.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: When you performed in Chicago, can you remember the very first nightclub you performed?
I think I worked either the 65 Club or the Day Swingland (?)
No, it was near South Park.
Did you have a cover charge, or people just came in?
Did they have a regular show or were you the main act?
I wasn’t the main act, but they let me play.
Did they have a dancer and MC? In those days, sometimes, they’d have an MC, a shake dancer, a comedian, then the musicians?
That’s what they had for you?
Do you remember how much a shot of whiskey was?
No, not really. Willie Bigtop says, there’s 20 shots in a bottle.
